title: GoTranscript Transcription Test
content_provenance: The domain names, weights and objectives are our own organisation of GoTranscript's public transcriber guidelines - the instructions the company tells applicants to read before taking its transcription test. GoTranscript publishes no exam blueprint and no domain weights, so the six equal-weight domains here group the guidelines' own sections (verbatim formats, timestamping and speaker labels, sound events and non-speech markings, numbers and times, dashes and quotation marks, the test job and ratings) so that a practice bank can be spread evenly across them.

exam.scoring: Practice bank: six sessions of 19 items, pass mark 70% per session. GoTranscript's own test is different: a guidelines quiz that must be passed with 100% correct (each question can have one or more correct answers), then a test job transcribed in clean verbatim with no timestamping. Live work is rated 5 (96-100% accuracy) down to 1 (0-82%), and three transcriptions with an average of 3.6 or lower mean removal from the transcriber team.

objectives.text: Full verbatim: the text is transcribed exactly as it sounds, including all the utterances of the speakers
Clean verbatim: speech errors, false starts (unless they add information), stutters, repetitions and filler words are removed
Expressions such as 'Oh my God' are kept regardless of verbatim type
Slang is expanded in clean verbatim: gotcha to got you, gonna to going to, wanna to want to, 'cause to because
'Yeah', 'yep', 'yap', 'yup' and 'mm-hmm' are written as 'yes'; 'alright' as 'all right'; 'Ok' and 'OK' as 'Okay'
Repetitions that express emphasis are kept; filler words that change the meaning of the phrase are kept
Affirmative and negative forms: Mm-hmm, Mm (affirmative) or Mm-mm (negative); Uh-huh (affirmative) or Uh-uh (negative)
Spoken contractions are never changed
Clean verbatim sentences avoid starting with a conjunction; expand the sentence instead
Timestamp format is [00:00:00] and timestamps are always bold
Timestamping types: every 2 minutes, or every time the speaker changes
Always consider the whole file when timestamping; embedded or burned-in time must be read from the downloaded file
Use the speaker's name from the audio or the file title, and always use a label even for one speaker
Make each speaker's role as descriptive as possible; the last name and titles may be dropped later in the file
Add a question mark before the label when the speaker cannot be identified
Labels are bold, followed by a colon and a space; never use the Tab button
Paragraphs are at most 500 symbols (about 100 words or 3-4 lines); lyrics are transcribed like a poem
Sentence divisions at conjunctions; every sentence ends with a punctuation mark and starts with a capital letter
Never use () instead of [], and never use exclamation marks
A comma before a coordinating conjunction that precedes an independent clause
[inaudible 00:00:00] when speech cannot be heard due to poor recording or noise (Ctrl + K)
[unintelligible 00:00:00] when speech can be heard but cannot be understood (Ctrl + I)
Only these two marks are allowed, they must not be invented, and they must specify the time
Sound events that are significant to the audio are noted in either format, in square brackets, without timestamps
Notes are in present or progressive tense, at most two words, grammatically correct and lower case
Sounds the speaker makes go on the same line; sounds not made by the speaker go on a separate line
[background noise], [crosstalk], [silence], [pause 00:00:00] and [sound cut] and where each one goes
[silence] covers 4 to 10 seconds; [pause 00:00:00] is for longer pauses, is bolded and always stands alone
Foreign language is marked [foreign language] or a named language; authors, titles and expressions are researched instead
Everything with a time-stamp is bolded, and nothing else besides speaker labels and timed marks is bolded
Square brackets are used for notes and marks; round brackets are never used
Single-digit numbers are spelled out; all other numbers use numerals
A sentence that mixes small and large numbers writes every number in numerals
Exceptions for readability: money, years and eras, age, percentages, measurements, equations, fractions, postal code, phone number and Bible citation
Money conversions: 1 grand is $1,000, 5 bucks is $5, 8 quid is £8, half a million dollars is $500,000
Times of day always capitalize AM and PM; with o'clock the numbers are spelled out
Nouns that are part of a series are capitalized (Grade 8, Section B, Chapter 1, Article VI); smaller divisions are not (page 1, paragraph 7)

sections.name: J - Double dashes and single dashes

objectives.text: Double dashes for a change of thought (false start), a speech error or an incomplete sentence
A single dash when the speech is interrupted but the speaker continues his thought
Full verbatim stutters and repetitions use a single dash
Direct quotations use double quotation marks and are introduced by a comma, not a colon
Commas and periods go inside the quotation marks; the question mark goes inside when the quotation itself is the question
Internal dialogues are direct quotations; indirect quotations take no quotation marks
The first word of a quoted complete sentence is capitalized
Italicize titles, artworks, plays, TV and radio programs and foreign expressions
Do not italicize social media sites, company names, the Bible, books within it or other sacred writings
Abbreviations and acronyms take no dashes or periods (USA, PhD); Dr., Mrs. in American English
Research proper capitalization (iPhone, UCLA, SaaS) and write links as www.facebook.com/groups/gotranscript

domains.name: The Test Job, Ratings and House Style

objectives.text: Part 1 is a guidelines quiz that must be passed with 100% correct; each question can have one or more correct answers
Part 2 is a test job transcribed in clean verbatim with no timestamping; read the provided instructions again first
The review of a submitted test job can take up to 60 days
Ratings run from 5 (96-100% accuracy) down to 1 (0-82%); editors rate accuracy, grammar and research
Three transcriptions with an average of 3.6 or lower mean removal; an average better than 4.5 opens the editor path
Not preparing transcriptions to the requirements can mean removal from the team of transcribers

sections.name: O - Work flow and house style

objectives.text: The flow: client upload, e-mail, transcription jobs page showing turnaround time, text format and timestamping type
Earnings on the stats page, payments every weekend on Friday, bad audio reported and refunded
US (American) spelling and Grammarly; et cetera is kept unless the client asks otherwise
Curse words are transcribed word for word
Customer dictated instructions are followed but never transcribed; spelled-out names are included except in dictation-type transcripts
Never paraphrase or correct the speaker, no [sic] tag, and use the correct spelling for misspoken words
